resolvedFailures.criterion: A role living in the environment this change renders can do its ordinary work in it — the spec's "What changes", and the pull request's own bullet "The repository's own cmd/legion test suite runs inside a role container again: its unix sockets no longer depend on TMPDIR being short". The suite a role runs is the repository's, not cmd/legion's alone.
resolvedFailures.evidence: `internal/shim` does not run under the TMPDIR this change gives a role container. In this issue's tester container, at the branch's code head, `cd packages/daemon && TMPDIR=/legion/scratch/implementer/tmp go test -count=1 -p 1 ./internal/shimwire/ ./internal/shim/ ./internal/stream/` fails with 16 `bind: invalid argument` listens, every one of them a socket this package's own helper spells under TMPDIR — for example `listen on /legion/scratch/implementer/tmp/TestAdoptWorkingCopyRunsTheSharedMetaeditAndAnswersTheDaemona_c240954141/003/s: bind: invalid argument` (shim_test.go:963), 110 bytes against Linux's 107-byte sun_path. The same command with TMPDIR=/tmp, which is what a role container had before this change (it was told no temporary directory at all), passes; `internal/shimwire` and `internal/stream` pass under both, and `cmd/legion` passes under both because this pull request already fixed it there (socketDir, worker_shim_test.go). So this is a regression this change introduces, in the same class the implementer recognised and fixed in one package: `internal/shim/shim_test.go:388`'s `socketPath` is `filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "s")`, the exact helper the pull request replaced in cmd/legion. The pull request's `Fast-follow:` line names `internal/daemon/daemon_test.go`'s `shortTempDir` and `internal/stream/helpers_test.go`'s `shortSocketPath` as the remaining copies; both of those in fact bind (stream's whole suite passes under the production TMPDIR), and the package that actually breaks is named nowhere. A defect that breaks a gate is not a fast-follow. Red test, in its own commit on this branch: `packages/daemon/internal/shim/socketpath_test.go`, `TestASocketPathBindsWhereTMPDIRIsARoleContainersScratch` — it points TMPDIR at a directory as long as a role container's and listens on the path `socketPath` builds, and fails today on any machine, CI included: `cd packages/daemon && go test -count=1 -run TestASocketPathBindsWhereTMPDIRIsARoleContainersScratch ./internal/shim/` prints `listen on /tmp/73b92639f15805283e38c12e76/TestASocketPathBindsWhereTMPDIRIsARoleContainersScratchAdoptWor2572775919/001/s (111 bytes): bind: invalid argument`. Rooting this package's socket directory at /tmp the way cmd/legion's socketDir does makes it pass.
resolvedFailures.notReproducedHere: `internal/daemon` could not be judged: its suite needs Docker (testcontainers panics `rootless Docker not found`) and a role container has none. Its `shortTempDir` builds `<TMPDIR>/lgdXXXXXXXXX/worker-stream.sock`, about 63 bytes under the rendered TMPDIR, so arithmetic says it fits; CI is where it is actually exercised, and CI runs with a short TMPDIR, so nothing here proves it either way. Round two read the premise under that arithmetic and it holds: every unix socket the package binds comes through `shortTempDir` — `testConfig`'s StateDir (daemon_test.go:84), which is where the worker stream's `unix://<StateDir>/worker-stream.sock` comes from, and `supervisor_test.go:157` — and the one config built on a bare `t.TempDir()` (clonecredential_test.go:53) calls `reconfigureCloneCredential` and listens on nothing.
resolvedFailures.fixedBy: bd2383dae192, `fix(daemon): the shim package's test socket binds under a role's TMPDIR`: socketPath makes the socket's own directory under /tmp and removes it with the test, as cmd/legion's socketDir already did; everything else a test writes stays under t.TempDir(). Verified in round two — see the proof entry `the repository's own suite runs under the TMPDIR this change renders`.

proof.criterion: The concurrency a shared Go cache rests on: the roles of one issue may build at once against one pair without corrupting it. Go's own documentation guarantees this of the build cache and says nothing of the module cache, so the module cache's half is proof or nothing.
proof.surface: the go toolchain in this issue's tester container, against one empty shared GOCACHE/GOMODCACHE pair on the issue's volume — the arrangement the runtime now renders
proof.command: with GOCACHE and GOMODCACHE pointed at an empty pair: two `go build ./...` of packages/daemon started at once and waited on, then a third `go build ./...`, then `go mod verify` (script and output at /legion/scratch/tester-live/conc.sh and conc.a, conc.b, conc.after, conc.verify)
proof.observed: Both concurrent builds exited 0. They did race rather than one waiting on the other: both logged the same module downloads (`go: downloading k8s.io/api v0.37.0` and some ninety more in each log), so both were filling the one module cache at the same time. The third build afterwards exited 0, and `go mod verify` answered `all modules verified` and exited 0, so nothing in the cache was left corrupt. The pair held 752 MB of build cache and 375 MB of module cache afterwards.
proof.negativeControl: `go mod verify` is the control for the module cache: it re-hashes every module in GOMODCACHE against go.sum and fails on any that does not match. That the commands do something is controlled too: the first attempt, with GOFLAGS=-mod=mod in the environment, refused before building at all and left a 4 KB build cache, so an exit 0 here is a build that ran.

proof.criterion: What sharing breaks is never the directory but a fixed name inside it: Playwright keeps one `ms-playwright` tree under the cache home, so two roles installing a browser at once write one path rather than two caches. Does it race?
proof.surface: the code that would run — playwright-core's own registry, fetched into a scratch directory here and read, since no Playwright is installed in this workspace
proof.command: bun add playwright-core into /legion/scratch/tester-live/pw, then read lib/coreBundle.js: the registry directory's derivation (line 34010-34022, 34465-34478) and Registry.install's lock (34883-34901)
proof.observed: It serialises rather than races, and the serialisation is explicit. The registry directory is `XDG_CACHE_HOME`/ms-playwright on Linux — `process.env.XDG_CACHE_HOME || path.join(os.homedir(), '.cache')`, then `+ '/ms-playwright'` — so the shared cache home does make one registry for all six roles, as the question assumes. `Registry.install()` then takes an exclusive directory lock before it writes anything: `lock(registryDirectory, {retries: {retries: 20, factor: 1.27579}, onCompromised, lockfilePath: <registryDirectory>/__dirlock})`, which is proper-lockfile's mutex, retried twenty times with exponential back-off over about ten minutes. So the second role's install waits for the first rather than writing into the same browser directory, and a holder that dies has its lock reclaimed as stale rather than wedging the directory. Two bounded consequences, neither a defect of this change: a second install that is still waiting after the back-off is spent fails with a lock error rather than proceeding, which with a ~400 MB download is unlikely but not impossible on a slow volume; and `install --force`, which removes a current installation before reinstalling, can now remove a browser tree another role of the issue is running from, where a cache home per role made that impossible. Oh My Pi's own browser is the image's `/usr/bin/chromium` and its profiles live under the state home, which stays the role's own, so the browser-broker rule is untouched by the sharing.
proof.negativeControl: the lock is read from the bundle that would actually execute, not from Playwright's documentation; the control on the premise is the derivation above — had the registry resolved to anything but XDG_CACHE_HOME the question would not arise, and it does resolve there.

proof.criterion: Nothing of Legion's own writes a fixed name into the four newly shared directories, where six roles of a pod now meet.
proof.command: grep -rnE 'TMPDIR[^)]*\)\s*\+|os\.TempDir\(\)' --include='*.go' packages/daemon and grep -rnE 'tmpdir\(\),\s*"[^"]+"' --include='*.ts' packages/*/src, excluding tests
proof.observed: Every temporary path Legion makes is unique by construction: each TypeScript site is `mkdtempSync`/`mkdtemp`, and the only two Go uses of `os.TempDir()` are `workspace-init fetch`'s and the repository cache's one-shot credential directory, both in containers whose TMPDIR is their own in-memory `/tmp` (fetchEnvironment, repocache.go) and never the role containers' shared scratch. The shared TMPDIR is also shorter than the per-role one it replaces — `/legion/scratch/tmp`, 19 bytes against 26-31 — so the sun_path headroom round one measured only grows.
proof.negativeControl: the grep is written to find the dangerous shape rather than the safe one — a fixed name joined to the temporary directory — and it does find the two `os.TempDir()` call sites, which is how their containers' TMPDIR came to be checked; it finds no such site in a role container's code path.
